🤖 Talos triage · confidence: medium

Talos can make mistakes. Please check important information.

Verdict
This looks like a known, already-analysed Izenda reporting slowness problem in our own code, with performance fixes written but switched off for each client until enabled; it is not a Tailored Brands data problem. I can't confirm from here that those fixes are enabled for this client.

What we checked

  • The client notes for Tailored Brands have nothing on reporting slowness, and the cross-client incident list has no matching entry.

  • The client's configuration files have no reporting-related settings, so nothing there is client-specific to this report tool.

  • An existing engineering write-up covers the same symptoms: slow report pages, timeouts and "server side" errors after the move to shared hosting.

  • The performance fixes from that write-up are switched off by default per client, so they change nothing until someone turns them on for that client.

  • The write-up records an open mismatch where users see a timeout at roughly two minutes while the underlying query keeps running for up to ten minutes. That fits "times out, then blank page, retry".

  • A separate setting can send this report tool to its own dedicated server. That setting is off by default after an earlier outage.

Next

  • Check whether the two Izenda performance settings and the dedicated-server routing setting are on or off for Tailored Brands in production.

  • Ask the customer for a few timestamps of slow or failed loads, so they can be matched against server logs and query times.

🤖 Talos triage · confidence: medium

Talos can make mistakes. Please check important information.

Verdict
No known or recurring incident matches, and nothing I read points to a code defect. The six users share a pattern (office, hub and distribution center staff), so the check is whether the sign-in data for them carries a level and a store assignment.

What we checked

  • Nothing in the client's notes or the cross-client known-incident list matches this symptom.

  • At each sign-in the security level is taken from the first of these that has a value: a level set in Secure's SSO admin screen, the level sent by the customer's sign-in system, or a configured default. If none has a value, the level stays blank.

  • No default level is set up for this client. The setting that would supply one is not present for Tailored Brands.

  • A user's store assignments are rebuilt at each sign-in from the store list the customer's sign-in system sends. If a user's sign-in carries no store, their store hierarchy stays empty. That fits the users who have no single store (office, hub, distribution center).

  • This client's setup maps users to Incident security levels by team membership. Users who are not in one of the listed teams would get no level from that mapping.

  • The "daily SSO file" is not something I could find in the code. I could not confirm which feed sets the level, and I could not see what was sent for these six users.

Next

  • Compare what the customer's sign-in system sent for one affected user (for example Chris Orth) with a user whose level and stores show correctly.

  • Check whether the six users are in a team listed in the client's Incident mapping, and whether their sign-in carries any store or hierarchy values.

Escalating to Secure Engineering. The Incident security level from SSO+ is not applied on the sign in that creates the user. Matthew Kamminga confirmed on Teams on 2026-10-15 that it should apply on creation and on later sign ins, and asked to route this to a new ENG ticket.

1. Environment and steps to reproduce

Production, tenant 209 tbi, sqldb-prd-wus2-arp-production-209-tbi-platform. Logs from Grafana Explore, grafanacloud-apprissretail-logs, clientId 209. Every query was read only.

Rachel Dill, 2026-10-13

  1. Her row exists in sso.SecurityLevelAssignments: SecurityID 5, Persistent NULL, loaded 2026-10-13 10:42 UTC. EXEC sso.GetUserSecurityLevel returns 5 for her.

  2. Her first SSO sign in, 2026-10-13 19:23:49 UTC, creates the account.

  3. Check membership.Users.SecurityID, or Portal, Settings, Users, Rachel Dill, Secure Incident tab.

Expected: Location Manager, SecurityID 5. Actual: NULL. I set it manually on 2026-10-14. It held after her next sign in on 2026-10-14 19:58 UTC.

2. Findings

Users created through SSO between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-15, all with level 5 in sso.SecurityLevelAssignments:

Every user who signed in again has the level. Every user whose only sign in created the account does not. Verified.

49 users who signed in since 2026-07-02 have a feed level above 0 and a NULL SecurityID in membership.Users and in the lpuser view. Verified. How many of them signed in only once is not checked yet.

My reading, unverified: the security level step is skipped on user creation and runs on later sign ins.

3. Troubleshooting performed

Ruled out so far: the feed, the rows are present; sso.GetUserSecurityLevel, its current definition orders by Persistent with no Persistent = 1 filter and returns 5; the lpuser view, every affected user is in it. Detail in my internal note of 2026-10-14 on https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-28256 .

Outside the ticket: Teams with Matthew Kamminga on 2026-10-15, and an email thread with J.R. Teagle on the same reports. Workaround in use: setting Incident Security ID manually in the Portal.

4. Still open

  1. Does the SSO user creation path call the security level assignment, and is that the step that is skipped?

  2. Once confirmed, could the affected accounts be corrected in one pass, or should Support set them one by one?

Related: https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-28256 and https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-27578 .
